recent_posts.title: Learning to love other people’s code.
recent_posts.summary: Working with legacy code you didn't write is a common developer challenge. A practical mindset shift involves asking 'why' before judging past decisions. Treating technical debt as archaeological clues, examining commit history and old tickets, and understanding the context of the era when code was written all help uncover the reasoning behind past choices. Approaching inherited code with empathy — recognizing constraints like time, budget, and skill level — leads to more informed decisions about whether to refactor, modernize, or leave things as they are.

recent_posts.title: What We Learned at NASPI
recent_posts.summary: A recap of the NASPI 2026 Work Group Meeting in Chicago, covering key themes in power grid modernization. Major topics included the impact of AI data center loads and inverter-based resources (IBRs) on grid stability, real-world deployments of PMU-based monitoring tools, next-generation analytics platforms like OPTIMA and FOLT, and a strong call for cross-utility data sharing to break down operational silos. The event also featured the authors' own Aion Pulse product at the vendor show.

recent_posts.title: Exploring the CIM Through the Organizations That Make It Happen
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into the organizations behind the Common Information Model (CIM) for power grid data standards. Covers CIMug (CIM Users Group) and its parent UCAIug, the IEC and its Technical Committee 57 (TC57) which publishes the formal CIM standards (IEC 61970, 61968, 62325), and ENTSO-E's role in mandating CIM adoption across the EU via CGMES. Also explains the relationship between the free/open-source UML ontological model maintained by CIMug and the proprietary IEC standards it generates.

recent_posts.title: What an Air Traffic Control Tower Taught Me About Software Design
recent_posts.summary: A visit to Phoenix Sky Harbor's air traffic control tower sparks reflection on software design philosophy. The TFDM system — a modern replacement for paper flight strips that looks like it was built for Windows 95 — illustrates why 'boring' interfaces often outperform flashy ones in high-stakes environments. The core argument: good software design means removing friction without disrupting the cognitive and social contracts users have built around existing workflows. Over-engineering (like AI-powered to-do apps) often serves the system rather than the user. The post also explores why cultural inertia (like keeping TRACON rooms dark even after the technical need disappeared) is a legitimate design consideration, not a failure.

recent_posts.title: Building a UX Research Brain: Atomic Research, Zettelkasten, and Obsidian
recent_posts.summary: Research Amnesia — repeatedly re-running studies your team already conducted — wastes budget and erodes stakeholder trust. A practical framework combining Atomic UX Research, the Zettelkasten note-linking method, and Obsidian is presented as a cure. Research is broken into four atom types: Studies, Research Questions, Facts, and Recommendations. Obsidian's bi-directional linking and graph view let Facts from one study automatically surface as evidence for questions in future studies. A 7-step workflow is detailed using a hypothetical onboarding research scenario, showing how raw session notes become standalone Fact notes linked to Research Questions, replacing bulky slide decks with a living, searchable knowledge graph stored in plain-text Markdown files the team fully owns.

recent_posts.title: Patterns of Knowing in Product Design
recent_posts.summary: Explores the epistemological foundations of UX design, drawing on philosopher Esther Lightcap Meek's concept of 'Subsidiary-Focal Integration' to explain how users learn digital tools. Argues that design patterns act like forest paths — familiar clues that help users move from intent to outcome without conscious effort. Emphasizes two guiding principles for designers: convention (leveraging widely recognized patterns to reduce learning curves) and consistency (maintaining those patterns reliably to build user trust). Design systems are presented as a practical mechanism for enforcing both principles across a product.

recent_posts.title: Build a custom tmux config from scratch with ergonomic key tables
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to building a custom tmux configuration from scratch, skipping the default 85+ bindings in favor of an ergonomic, menu-driven key table system. Covers core tmux concepts (sessions, windows, panes, key tables, formats), how to unbind defaults and create hierarchical key bindings using the Meta key, conditional pane navigation with format variables, copy mode setup, buffer management, nested tmux handling, and useful configuration options like base-index and status line customization.

recent_posts.title: Automating Grid Reliability
recent_posts.summary: Modern electric grids face growing reliability challenges as inverter-based resources (IBRs) like wind, solar, and battery storage replace traditional synchronous generators. Manual generator performance verification using PMU data is no longer scalable given the frequency of disturbances and fleet sizes. Regulatory frameworks including NERC BAL-003-2 and FERC Orders 842 and 901 mandate rigorous frequency and voltage response monitoring. Automated tools that process PMU and SCADA time-series data can detect events, quantify frequency response measures (FRM), evaluate droop behavior, and track voltage response measures (VRM) across entire fleets in near-real time. Aion Pulse, developed by Simple Thread in collaboration with PNNL and funded by the U.S. DOE, commercializes the Generator Scorecard research tool to deliver these capabilities, reducing engineering workload and improving NERC compliance.

recent_posts.title: Using computer vision and logistic regression to predict chicken egg hatchability
recent_posts.summary: A data scientist applies computer vision and logistic regression to predict chicken egg hatchability in a personal homesteading project. Using a Kaggle dataset of 4,000+ candled egg images, a CNN was trained achieving 96% accuracy and 0.91 AUC. The model assigned fertility probabilities to 18 named eggs across incubation days, which were combined with physical measurements (shell porosity, weight loss, cleanliness) into a composite viability score. Eggs were grouped into narrative categories: Minor Characters, Cliffhangers, and Protagonists. Of 18 eggs, 10 hatched. The logistic regression model showed strong alignment with true outcomes, with no false negatives, though small sample size limited generalizability. The experiment highlights how deep learning, quantitative analysis, and human judgment each contribute uniquely to prediction tasks.

recent_posts.title: From Figma to Production: Creating Designs Developers Love
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide for UI designers on creating Figma files that developers can easily implement. Covers consistent naming conventions that mirror code patterns, proper use of auto layout to reflect how interfaces are built in code, explicit design specs using design tokens, in-file documentation of design decisions, mapping interaction states and user flows, and the importance of early developer collaboration throughout the design process.

top_posts.title: Docker Approaches to Multiple Environments
top_posts.summary: Explores two strategies for managing Docker configurations across development, staging, and production environments. The first approach uses separate Dockerfiles for each environment (similar to Rails configuration patterns), while the second leverages Docker's multi-stage builds to handle multiple environments within a single Dockerfile. Compares the trade-offs between explicit separation versus DRY principles, helping teams choose the right approach based on their complexity needs and Docker expertise.

top_posts.title: How to Accomplish Things When You Are Not Feeling It
top_posts.summary: Feeling unmotivated on cold, dreary days is common, but with a few strategic tips, you can stay productive. Organize your week using a paper calendar to visualize tasks. Start with the easiest task on your list to build momentum. Break down larger projects into smaller, manageable pieces. Allow yourself to start tasks without the pressure of finishing them immediately. If all else fails, take a break to do a household chore to reset your mind. These approaches can help turn even the hardest moments into opportunities for progress.

top_posts.title: Unnecessary Anxiety in Software Development
top_posts.summary: Software development often creates unnecessary anxiety through risky practices like deploying without proper safeguards. Using a metaphor of walking across a plank between buildings, the author explains how anxiety is self-reinforcing and leads to avoidance behaviors. Organizations can reduce developer stress by implementing better testing, staging environments, documentation, and blameless cultures. Individuals can combat anxiety by approaching feared tasks, building competence, and accepting discomfort as part of growth. The key is lowering both the likelihood of failure and its consequences.

top_posts.title: Web Standards Are Cool Again
top_posts.summary: Remix is the latest open-source, fullstack, web development framework to hit the npm registry. It couples web fundamentals like the client/server model, HTTP caching, and native HTML forms with modern UI tools like dynamic page refreshing, nested routing, and React to create a truly remarkable way for developers to create fast, interactive, and portable user experiences.

top_posts.title: Our Favorite Books of 2024
top_posts.summary: The Simple Thread team shares their favorite books of 2024, featuring a diverse range of genres and styles. Highlights include Corban Addison's narrative non-fiction Wastelands, John Ganz's political history The Year The Clock Broke, and Nick Cutter's horror fiction The Troop. Each recommendation embodies different themes, from environmental justice and political crises to survival and self-improvement, offering something for every reader's taste.
